title: Scientificness
description: This paper proposes a generalized framework for scientific method rooted in internal coherence, ontological clarity, and structural justification. It argues that scientific inquiry cannot be reduced to empirical modeling or bias-avoidance heuristics. Rather, science begins with an act of boundary-setting: what counts as a legitimate subject, object, and field. Drawing from examples in physics, law, and epistemology, the paper critiques the misuse of models whose assumptions are not matched to their claims, and offers an alternative approach based on coherence-testing of claims against domain-specific structural constraints. A method is sketched for evaluating scientific claims through structured "model cards" that track key theories, ontological commitments, and logical implications, enabling cross-paper comparison and interdisciplinary synthesis. The scientific method, thus redefined, becomes a constraint logic applied to purpose-driven domains — not a set of generic procedures, but a way of thinking clearly under defined limits. Through cross-domain analysis, a deep isomorphism is revealed between scientific and legal reasoning, both functioning as structured systems for decision-making under uncertainty. Extending this logic, we propose practical instruments to audit knowledge claims for structural integrity. This has implications not only for natural science but also for the legitimacy of legal, social, and institutional reasoning.
